reasons: When the industry context is missing, the code falls back to defaults that can produce broken links.

terms.meaning: A trail of links showing where the current page sits in the app.
A chosen slice of an industry, such as one part of its market, that filters pages.
The sign-in system that identifies users and their roles.
Shared information about the current industry, provided to components by a hook.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports the header pieces
sections.what: Brings in the router helpers, icons, sign-in and industry hooks, the segment helper, the brand name and the theme toggle.
sections.why: Likely reason: the header is built from these parts.

sections.name: TopNav (part 1)
sections.title: Tab list and segment carry-over
sections.what: Reads the user role and the current industry, carries the chosen segment into the Explore, Analysis and Pipeline links, and builds the tab list. Admin-only tabs are added for admins. It also sets up the industry name and home link for the breadcrumb.
sections.why: Stated in the code: the segment scope is carried across the workspace pages that honour it.
sections.watch_out: Several tab links are built from the industry slug, so a missing slug produces a broken link.

sections.name: TopNav (part 2)
sections.title: Quick links, user badge and tab row
sections.what: Draws the logo and breadcrumb, the All industries, Tools and Industries links, the theme toggle and the signed-in user badge, with a sign-out button when sign-in is on. Below that, it draws the row of workspace tabs and underlines the one for the current page.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the main ways to move around the app visible on every page.
sections.watch_out: The badge shows the raw user identifier and role to anyone looking at the screen, and the tab highlight needs an exact address match, so a sub-page does not highlight its parent tab.

summary: The top bar of each industry workspace. It shows breadcrumbs, links to other areas, the workspace tabs and the signed-in user.
purpose: Lets users move between the industry home, all industries, tools and workspace pages such as Explore, Pipeline and Map, and shows who is signed in.
why: Reason not stated in the code for the layout. The header is shared so the same navigation appears on each page.
how: 1. Reads the signed-in user and the current industry. 2. Builds the tab list, adding admin-only tabs for admins. 3. Carries the chosen segment into the Explore, Analysis and Pipeline links. 4. Draws the breadcrumb, quick links, theme toggle and user badge. 5. Draws the tab row and highlights the tab for the current page.
inputs: The signed-in user, the industry context, the active segment, and the current page address and search text.
outputs: A navigation header with links. A sign-out button appears when sign-in is enabled.
risks: The user identifier is shown as plain text. Sign-out appears only when authentication is enabled.
debug: If tabs are missing, check the industry context and the user role. If a tab is not highlighted, check that the address matches exactly. If links contain undefined, the industry context is missing.
